phase: DEV-248 River Development Agent Controlled Executor Capability Authorization Foundation
commitMessage: DEV-248: Build River Development Agent controlled executor capability authorization foundation
architectureStatus: Generation III controlled executor capability authorization foundation
predecessor: DEV-247 River Development Agent controlled executor capability foundation
objective: Create a deterministic controlled executor capability-authorization foundation that consumes a trusted ready DEV-247 controlled executor capability record and derives an explicit fail-closed authorization decision over only the capabilities already eligible within the inherited approved execution scope, while preserving execution-request provenance, human authorization evidence, repository authorization evidence, explicit approval evidence, capability eligibility evidence, and strict separation between capability authorization and actual execution.
architecturalDecision: DEV-247 establishes deny-by-default capability eligibility without authorization or execution.
DEV-248 introduces a separate capability-authorization boundary before any downstream controlled executor operation.
Only capabilities already eligible in DEV-247 may become authorized.
Capability authorization cannot create capabilities absent from the DEV-247 eligible capability set.
Capability authorization remains request-specific and scope-bound.
Authorization does not perform command execution or repository mutation.
Authorization cannot create commit, push, deployment, secret-access, autonomous-execution, or scope-expansion authority.
Actual executor operations remain downstream and separately governed.
invariants: Capability authorization requires trusted DEV-247 capability evidence.
Capability authorization requires ready DEV-247 capability evidence.
Capability authorization requires preserved authorization evidence.
Capability authorization requires executor admission.
Capability authorization requires an unblocked predecessor record.
Capability authorization requires governed execution-request evidence.
Capability authorization requires at least one eligible capability.
Capability authorization is deny-by-default.
Only DEV-247 eligible capabilities may be authorized.
Capability authorization cannot create new capabilities.
Capability authorization cannot expand approved execution scope.
Capability authorization preserves human authorization evidence.
Capability authorization preserves repository authorization evidence.
Capability authorization preserves explicit approval evidence.
Capability authorization preserves capability eligibility evidence.
Capability authorization does not imply command execution.
Capability authorization does not imply repository modification.
Capability authorization does not imply repository deletion.
Capability authorization does not imply commit authority.
Capability authorization does not imply push authority.
Capability authorization does not imply deployment authority.
Capability authorization does not imply secret access.
Capability authorization does not imply autonomous execution.
